page: Amazon Web Services i3.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz, featuring 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 244.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.62 GB per core, and a 45 MB L3 cache. Storage is a key feature of this instance, which comes bundled with 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile with distinct tradeoffs. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU, bzip3 decompression single-threaded, and Geekbench single-core scores all falling into the bottom 10% of tested servers. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and large-block memory write bandwidth are weak, placing in the bottom 25%. However, multi-threaded performance is more robust, with multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression all achieving average tier results. Database operations, Redis SET operations at 20.29 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 16.35 GB/sec also perform in the average range, demonstrating the instance's capacity for parallelized workloads despite its weak single-core execution.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i3.8xlarge offers high local storage density and substantial memory capacity relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads that require high-capacity local NVMe storage without needing the latest generation of high-frequency CPU cores. The instance is well-suited for storage-heavy and parallelized workloads such as relational and non-relational databases, distributed file systems, data warehousing, and caching layers like Redis. It is less suitable for single-threaded processing tasks or compute-heavy workloads that depend on high single-core clock speeds or advanced vector instructions.
